lessonContentPlans.lessonSummary: Introduce the major systems, professional expectations, safety boundaries, technical-information habits, and evidence-based reasoning process learners will use throughout the automotive technology curriculum.
prerequisites: Orientation to the AutoLearnPro learning environment

learningObjectives.statement: Identify major vehicle systems and explain their basic functional relationships without treating a system overview as a vehicle-specific service procedure.
Distinguish a customer concern, observation, measurement, technical reference, hypothesis, and diagnostic conclusion.
Use safety, professional practice, and applicable technical information to select and document an appropriate next step for a basic vehicle concern.

contentBlocks.title: Lesson targets
contentBlocks.description: Preview the systems, evidence, safety, and professional-practice outcomes for the lesson.

contentBlocks.title: What learners already know
contentBlocks.description: Activate everyday vehicle knowledge while separating informal familiarity from verified technical information.

contentBlocks.title: Vehicle systems as an interconnected whole
contentBlocks.description: Introduce major vehicle systems and the idea that a symptom in one area may depend on conditions in another.

contentBlocks.title: Vehicle-system relationship model
contentBlocks.description: Use a simplified conceptual model to connect power, control, chassis, thermal, electrical, and information functions without implying a universal vehicle architecture.

contentBlocks.title: From concern to next step
contentBlocks.description: Demonstrate how a basic vehicle concern moves from reported symptom to observation, information gathering, hypothesis, and a justified next check.

contentBlocks.title: Evidence sorting
contentBlocks.description: Classify sample statements as concern, observation, measurement, reference, hypothesis, or conclusion.

contentBlocks.title: Basic vehicle concern
contentBlocks.description: Choose a safe and information-supported next step for a simple vehicle concern without being given a repair answer.

contentBlocks.title: Foundations reasoning check
contentBlocks.description: Use low-stakes formative prompts to check system recognition, evidence classification, and next-step reasoning.

contentBlocks.title: Explain and retry
contentBlocks.description: Provide reasoning-focused feedback and allow revision without creating scored assessment eligibility.

contentBlocks.title: Technical information and source boundary
contentBlocks.description: Reinforce that vehicle-specific procedures, specifications, limits, and safety instructions require applicable authoritative information.

contentBlocks.title: Foundations summary
contentBlocks.description: Summarize how systems thinking, safety, professional practice, evidence, and documentation support later automotive coursework.

visuals.title: Major vehicle-system relationships
visuals.purpose: Show high-level relationships among vehicle systems without presenting a vehicle-specific schematic.

visuals.title: Concern-to-next-step workflow
visuals.purpose: Show the sequence from concern through evidence gathering and documentation.

visuals.title: Evidence versus conclusion
visuals.purpose: Compare concerns, observations, measurements, references, hypotheses, and conclusions.

visuals.title: Automotive learning foundations
visuals.purpose: Summarize systems thinking, safety, professional practice, evidence, technical information, and documentation.

practiceTasks: Match common vehicle functions to the major system most directly responsible for them
Sort sample statements into concern, observation, measurement, reference, hypothesis, or conclusion
Identify which information must be verified before following a vehicle-specific procedure
Write a brief rationale for a safe next step in a basic guided concern
lessonContentPlans.evidenceExpectation: Technical claims require approved provenance. Vehicle-specific procedures, values, limits, and specifications require an appropriate authoritative source and must not be invented.
lessonContentPlans.assessmentBoundary: Training checks may coach, explain, and allow retry. Scored assessment remains a separate approval state and requires provenance, review status, curriculum mapping, and secure delivery.
